text:
sara: Heads-up — ACME customer reported a burst of p95/p99 latency on their eu-west dedicated pool + lots of 429s between 09:12-09:18 UTC. They say autoscale did not add slices. Suspect noisy-neighbor MIG contention on a mixed-config host. Filing here to triage :warning:

devon: @sara can you paste the tenant id and the sample trace/logs? Also which model/seq len were they hitting? :eyes:

sara: Tenant: acme-prod-42. Model: rwf-13b (quant-8), typical seq=512. Repro curl we used to generate load: ```
curl -s -X POST
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  https://api.eu-west.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -d '{"model":"rwf-13b","input":"x"*512,"max_tokens":256,"stream":false}'
```

sara: Snippet of the client's error stream: ```
[2026-03-10T09:12:05Z] 429 Too Many Requests - client burst
[2026-03-10T09:12:06Z] RPC error: context deadline exceeded
[2026-03-10T09:12:07Z] p95 latency: 1.8s (baseline ~220ms)
[2026-03-10T09:15:00Z] p99 latency: 4.3s
```

autoscale-bot: Autoscale events for pool eu-west-dedicated-8 between 09:00-09:30:
  - 09:00:00 scale=4
  - 09:05:00 cpu_load=0.48, gpu_queue=0.12
  - 09:10:00 cpu_load=0.86, gpu_queue=0.65 -> policy: check_thresholds
  - 09:11:30 attempted_scale_up but rate_limit for slice-alloc reached
  - 09:14:00 scale_up_blocked: fragment_alloc_fail

mike: If scale_up was blocked by fragment_alloc_fail, sounds like we couldn't place a full MIG slice. What was the host packing config? Fractional MIG or mixed counts?

sara: Host shows mixed partitions: some 1g/2g/3g slices, we put this tenant on a 3g slice. But logs show another tenant on same physical node with sudden SM saturation. Link to node metrics: https://internal-metrics/eu-west/node-az3/host-7293

julia: Can you check DCGM metrics for SM utilization / memory bw / L3 misses for the time window? If SM% and SM Active Cycles spike, it's classic noisy neighbor. Also look for large memcpy or kernel launches from other slices. Suggest running: ```
# quick DCGM query (privileged)
dcgmstats --query sm_util,mem_bw,pcie_bw --start 2026-03-10T09:10:00 --end 2026-03-10T09:18:00 host-7293
```

opsbot: Collected dcgm snapshots (attached to ticket RDW-4892). Noted: host-7293 SM util peaked at 98% for ~90s, memory bw also maxed. Kernel pattern shows many short-lived high-concurrency kernels from tenant "sprint-labs" on the same host.

kevin: Mitigation options: (1) Migrate acme-prod-42 to an isolated slice on a different host (manual drain + allocate) — fast but billing will pro-rate slice. (2) Force a canary pin to a compatible model variant that's less SM heavy (e.g., rwf-13b-int8) while we investigate. (3) Temporarily enable strict packing policy to avoid mixed partitions on dense hosts.

sara: Tried (1) — requested migration at 09:20, migration failed with fragment_alloc_fail again. Ops says the cluster is fragmented.

mike: Long-term fix: we need to improve fractional packing heuristics and preemptive defragmentation. Short-term: escalate to infra to trigger a proactive drain of highly-fragmented hosts and allow compaction. I'll open infra-ops ticket.

devon: For the customer reply: give them a concise summary + ETA. Suggested message: "We're seeing a colocated tenant causing GPU saturation on the host. We're moving you to an isolated slice; temporary pro-rate may apply. We expect migration within 2 hours; will update." Thoughts?

sara: Sounds good. I'll send that and include the mitigation options offered. Also adding notes to RDW-4892 with timing and DCGM outputs. :thumbsup:

kevin: Follow-ups: 1) Confirm whether packing policy change should be rolled cluster-wide or per-az. 2) Add a metric/alert for 'fragment_alloc_fail' rate so autoscale decisions consider allocation failures. 3) Consider a fast-path emergency fallback that routes traffic to alternate region when scale up is blocked.

sara: Thanks all. Adding action items to the ticket and scheduling a quick sync with infra in 30m. If anyone sees additional logs, paste them here.
